title: The boundary miss
context: A developer asked an AI assistant to slice a results array into pages of 10 items for a paginated table. The suggested code compiles and looks reasonable, but every page is missing its last row, and users keep reporting gaps between pages.
question: Why does every page returned by getPage have only 9 items instead of 10?
options: Array.prototype.slice's end argument is already exclusive, so subtracting 1 excludes the page's true last item.
pageNumber should start counting from 0, not 1.
pageSize only defaults to 10 when the argument is undefined, not when it's 0.
start is computed before pageNumber is validated as a positive integer.

explanation.theBug: Array.prototype.slice(start, end) already treats end as exclusive — it returns elements up to but not including index end. Subtracting 1 from end double-applies that exclusivity, dropping the true last item of every page. For a pageSize of 10, slice(start, start + 10) is correct; slice(start, start + 9) silently returns only 9 items.
explanation.whyAIGeneratesThis: The model conflates 'inclusive last index' math — common when writing raw for-loops with <= — with slice's argument semantics, which are exclusive by design. Because the -1 adjustment is exactly the fix you'd need for a loop condition, it gets applied here out of habit even though slice doesn't need it.

theFix.before:
const end = start + pageSize - 1;
  return items.slice(start, end);
theFix.after:
const end = start + pageSize;
  return items.slice(start, end);
theFix.commentary: slice's end parameter is already exclusive — no -1 adjustment is needed, or wanted.

explanation.reviewHeuristic: Before adjusting an index by plus or minus one, check whether the API you're calling is already inclusive or exclusive at that boundary — stacking your own adjustment on top of the API's is how off-by-one bugs sneak in.
